title: Modi Signed 19 Agreements in Seychelles Today. Here's What India Got — and What It Gave.
excerpt: A warship, UPI for the island nation, an extradition treaty, a space cooperation pact, 500 tonnes of rice, and a plan to build a national hospital — all in one afternoon on a 115-island archipelago.
body:
When Prime Minister Narendra Modi sat down with Seychelles President Patrick Herminie at the State House in Victoria on Sunday, the two leaders had a lot to sign. By the time they stood up, India and Seychelles had unveiled **19 formal outcomes** — spanning defence, digital payments, space cooperation, healthcare, agriculture, education and extradition.

The scope of the agreements is disproportionate to Seychelles' size — a 115-island archipelago with a population of roughly 100,000. But that is precisely the point. For India, Seychelles is not a small country. It is a strategically located partner in the Indian Ocean, where China has been spending aggressively on port deals, military basing and infrastructure diplomacy for years.

## What India Gave

The centrepiece of the defence package was the handover of **PS Lespwar**, a 52-metre Fast Patrol Vessel built by Goa Shipyard Limited. The ship is designed to boost Seychelles' maritime surveillance and Exclusive Economic Zone patrol capabilities — a domain where India has been systematically building partnerships across the Indian Ocean rim.

India also handed over **10 utility vehicles**, **five Laser Radial class boats** to the Seychelles Defence Force, completed the **refit of PS Zoroaster** (a Seychelles Coast Guard patrol vessel), and supplied a **glass cockpit upgrade for a Dornier aircraft** used by Seychelles' forces.

On the civilian side, India delivered **six ambulances**, **500 metric tonnes of rice**, and **8,500 metric tonnes of cement** — the kind of unglamorous, material support that builds goodwill in ways infrastructure loans do not.

## What They Signed

The 19 outcomes included:

**Security & Legal:** An extradition treaty — a significant step signalling the deepening of legal cooperation.

**Space:** An agreement on cooperation in the peaceful uses of outer space, opening a new dimension in bilateral ties.

**Digital Payments:** NPCI International Payments Ltd. and the Central Bank of Seychelles signed an agreement to deploy **UPI-based digital payments** across the country. This extends India's flagship payment system — already live in Singapore, the UAE, Sri Lanka, Bhutan and Mauritius — into another Indian Ocean nation.

**Finance:** An umbrella **Line of Credit agreement** worth ₹1,250 crore with the Export-Import Bank of India, giving Seychelles access to Indian capital for development projects.

**Healthcare:** An MoU between HLL Lifecare Ltd. and Seychelles' health ministry under the **Jan Aushadhi scheme** — India's generic-medicine programme — to supply affordable Indian medicines. A separate agreement for preliminary preparations for a **new Seychelles National Hospital**.

**Education & Capacity Building:** A virtual ground-breaking ceremony for a **Professional and Technical Education Centre**. Agreements on diplomatic training between India's Sushma Swaraj Institute of Foreign Service and Seychelles' Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and on agriculture research and education.

**Maritime:** Recognition of training and certification of seafarers on Seychelles-flagged vessels — a practical step for Indian maritime professionals.

## The Strategic Map

Modi's visit — his first to Seychelles since 2015 — coincided with the **50th anniversary of India-Seychelles diplomatic relations** and the Golden Jubilee of Seychelles' National Day. He arrived as Guest of Honour, accompanied by a contingent of Indian defence forces and two Indian Navy ships.

The visit is framed by Modi's **"Vision MAHASAGAR"** — *Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and Growth Across Regions* — India's umbrella doctrine for Indian Ocean engagement. Since 2015, India has gifted patrol vessels to Seychelles, Mauritius and the Maldives, established coastal radar networks, and trained coast guard personnel across the region.

Seychelles occupies a commanding position in the western Indian Ocean, astride shipping lanes connecting the Gulf, East Africa and South Asia. Its Exclusive Economic Zone of 1.3 million square kilometres is disproportionate to its land area, making maritime surveillance a shared interest.

"Our partnership in the health sector has stood the test of time," Modi said, referencing India's vaccine supply during the COVID-19 pandemic. The MoUs signed today, he added, would bring that partnership into new domains.

For the diaspora spread across the Indian Ocean rim — in the Gulf, East Africa and Southeast Asia — India's growing security and economic footprint in the region is more than foreign policy. It is infrastructure that connects their worlds. UPI in Seychelles is a convenience for Indian tourists and a statement of digital-ecosystem ambition. A patrol vessel in Victoria harbour is a signal to every power watching the Indian Ocean that New Delhi intends to stay.
